title: Texts, learning, and prestige
paragraphs: The examination system made education politically valuable in distinctive ways. Literary competence could serve as a sign of refinement and administrative promise. Students worked within traditions of classical learning that connected Goryeo to a larger East Asian intellectual world. Mastery of texts was a cultural accomplishment as well as a route toward institutional influence.

Such learning required time and support. The student reading at night was part of a larger household economy that made sustained study possible. Asking who could afford that investment reveals the social conditions behind the appealing ideal of office earned through learning.
